instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and principals must register under §13.64, so the statute requires all paid lobbyists to register/license.

Section 13.695(2) requires changes in the name of an officer/employee or general area of legislative action disclosed in a statement to be reported in writing to the commission within 10 days of the change; §13.64(3) similarly requires written notice before lobbying in any new area not previously filed.

Section 13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless already licensed and authorized, and §13.65 requires the authorization to be filed BEFORE engaging in lobbying — so the lobbyist's deadline is pre-lobbying (zero days after initial lobbying is permitted).

The lobbyist files a license application under §13.63(1)(a), the principal separately files a registration statement under §13.64(1), and a separate authorization under §13.65 is required for each principal-lobbyist pairing — three separate filings rather than one combined form.

Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the required application contents (social security number, residence address option, signature, fee) and §13.685(1) tasks the commission with prescribing forms, with no mention of a photograph requirement anywhere in the statute.

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity, and §13.621(1)(d) exempts agency-to-agency lobbying.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under §13.695 and its named officials are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 (except as provided in §13.695), creating a partial exemption from the requirements applied to non-government principals/lobbyists.
